analysis:
Reviewed all supplied metadata, patches and source excerpts. DeviceLinkForm.tsx now accepts provider/desktop_account purpose (head patch line 9), sends it with the authenticated approval request (head 45), and refuses desktop success messaging unless the coordinator acknowledges desktop_account (head 62). It adds read-only/30-day consent language (head 217); this is a UI claim, not enforcement. Existing token acquisition, explicit user submission, code normalization and error handling remain. account-proxy-contracts.test.ts head 55–62 tests raw purpose forwarding and acknowledgment using a mocked upstream. device-link.test.tsx head 50–105 tests default provider purpose, desktop consent, missing acknowledgment, retries and missing token; pages.test.tsx head 12 only adds a navigation mock. Changelog line 3 describes the intended console behavior, not deployment proof.
Relevant external contract: A-008 provider credentials and TB-011/T-053 credential/authorization lifecycle; no supplied changes to attestation, inference encryption, cache isolation, privileged helper, artifact qualification or billing controls. No concrete regression established in these units. Integration must examine link/page purpose parsing and component lifecycle, the actual approval proxy, and platform-side binding of purpose to issued code/token and endpoint permissions. Those implementations are absent here; mocked responses cannot establish that desktop credentials really lack provider, key-management and withdrawal authority or expire after 30 days. Canonical context excludes backend/console implementation and supplies only selected definition details.
